info.title: Postroom API
info.description: REST/JSON under /api for the Postroom webmail. Generated from the zod schemas that validate requests (PST-REQ-085); regenerate with `pnpm --filter @postroom/api openapi`.

hasPhoto.description: The card carries a PHOTO; kept on edit, not editable here.

name.description: The card’s resource name in its address book.

id.description: The draft’s message id. A save replaces the draft, so this changes every save.

editable.description: False when the rule uses parts the web form cannot show.

name.description: The event’s resource name in its calendar.

endDay.description: All-day only: the day after the last.

highestModseq.description: A MODSEQ (RFC 7162), as a decimal string.
A MODSEQ (RFC 7162), as a decimal string.

messageId.description: The Message-ID header of the MDN that was sent.

html.description: The HTML part exactly as sent. NOT sanitised: render it only on the usercontent origin (PST-T-3.12).

modseq.description: A MODSEQ (RFC 7162), as a decimal string.

trashedAt.description: When the message entered Trash (the retention clock); null outside Trash.

expiresAt.description: When the retention sweep expunges it from Trash; null outside Trash or when Trash keeps mail forever.

source.description: Where the verdicts came from: the filed message's verdict, the spool row, or nowhere (e.g. your own Sent copy).

alignment.description: Alignment with the From domain as DMARC's evaluator stated it in its reasons; null when it did not say.
Alignment with the From domain as DMARC's evaluator stated it in its reasons; null when it did not say.

arcOverride.description: Why a trusted ARC sealer overrode a DMARC failure, when it did.

authenticationResults.description: Every Authentication-Results field in the message, top first (RFC 8601).

with.description: The protocol (RFC 5321 §4.4, RFC 3848): ESMTPS means the hop was encrypted.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds since the previous (older) hop; null for the first or when either date is unreadable.

received.description: The Received path, oldest hop first.

smtpReply.description: The SMTP reply smtp-in actually sent at the end of DATA.

receipt.description: What smtp-in recorded about the session that delivered it here; null for mail that did not arrive over SMTP.

scores.description: Every score stored with the decision (PST-REQ-103), by name.

signals.description: The rule classifier's signals (bulk, automated, human, transactional, …).

html.description: Whether the message has an HTML part at all.

returnPathMatches.description: RFC 8098 §2.1: a receipt to an address other than Return-Path needs the reader's say-so.

sent.description: Postroom never sends a receipt on its own; sending one is a separate, explicit step (PST-T-9.2).

status.description: 'verified-known-key' (valid, and the key is one of this account's own or contact keys) | 'valid-signature-unknown-key' (valid, but the key or certificate came only with the message) | 'bad-signature' | 'not-signed' | 'unsupported:<reason>'. A signature that verifies is still unsupported, never verified, when it is not a document signature ('unsupported:signature-type-0xNN'), its key is revoked or expired ('key-revoked', 'key-expired'), it expired or is dated in the future ('signature-expired', 'signature-from-future'), or — S/MIME — it uses SHA-1 ('weak-hash-sha1'), its certificate was outside its validity window ('certificate-expired') or is not for e-mail ('certificate-not-for-email'), or its encoding is not DER ('ber-encoding', 'signed-attributes-not-der').

keyId.description: OpenPGP key ID, or the certificate serial number.

fingerprint.description: OpenPGP v4 fingerprint, or the certificate SHA-256.

userIds.description: User IDs of the key, or the certificate subject.

addresses.description: Addresses the key or certificate speaks for (rfc822Name for S/MIME).

fromMatches.description: Whether the From address is one of `addresses`; null when either is unknown.

keySource.description: Where the key came from: this account's keys, the message itself (never trusted on its own), or nowhere.

signatureVerified.description: Signed by the next certificate presented (or by itself, when self-signed).

certificates.description: S/MIME: the certificate chain as presented in the message, signer first.

chain.description: Whether the chain verifies up to what the message carried. No system trust store is consulted.

crypto.description: PGP/MIME, inline PGP and S/MIME signature and decryption status (PST-REQ-160).

modseq.description: A MODSEQ (RFC 7162), as a decimal string.

trashedAt.description: When the message entered Trash (the retention clock); null outside Trash.

expiresAt.description: When the retention sweep expunges it from Trash; null outside Trash or when Trash keeps mail forever.

kind.description: undo: held for the undo window; scheduled: a chosen send time.

releaseAt.description: When the worker queues it (within a minute of this).

draftId.description: The copy in Drafts; it stays there while held, and after an undo.

to.description: The To and Cc addresses, space-separated.

messageId.description: The Message-ID header it will be sent with.

reason.description: Why it was cancelled or failed.

url.description: The sanitised message on the usercontent origin: frame it with sandbox (no allow-scripts, no allow-same-origin). A capability; expires at expiresAt.

images.description: Whether remote images load (through the proxy) in this render.

remoteImages.description: Remote images in the message. Above 0 with images false means some are blocked.

trackersBlocked.description: Known tracking pixels dropped entirely from this message, never loaded even with images on (PST-REQ-116).

linksCleaned.description: Links with a tracking parameter stripped or a known redirect wrapper unwrapped (PST-REQ-116).

messageId.description: The Message-ID header of the sent message.

threadId.description: The thread the Sent copy joined (null only if threading failed; the sweep retries).

reminderId.description: The remind-if-no-reply armed for it, when one was asked for.

messageIds.description: The messages moved out of INBOX (their ids do not change).

post.summary: Send a message through the submission path, and file it in Sent.
post.description: Builds a strict-CRLF RFC 5322 message (text/plain UTF-8, encoded-words for non-ASCII headers; a forward attaches the original as message/rfc822) and runs it through the same submission path as SMTP on 587/465: From must be one of the caller’s addresses, it is DKIM-signed, the recipient cap is enforced, and it is queued and audited — then filed in Sent in the same transaction and threaded. A draftId is removed from Drafts in that transaction.

undoSeconds.description: Undo send: hold the message this many seconds before it is queued (0–30; the webmail sends its setting, default 10). Absent or 0 sends at once.

sendAt.description: Scheduled send: hold the message until this time, then queue it (within a minute). Not with undoSeconds.

remindAfterSeconds.description: Remind if no reply: when nobody else has written in the thread this long after it was sent, it comes back to INBOX.

202.description: Held (undoSeconds > 0 or sendAt): a copy is in Drafts and the worker queues it at releaseAt, unless it is undone first.

Live updates as server-sent events.
get.description: Starts with one mailbox.changed per mailbox, then message.new (MessageNewEvent) and mailbox.changed (MailboxChangedEvent) as mail arrives or changes. A comment heartbeat every 25 s. Only the caller's mailboxes.

post.summary: Start a full-data export of the caller's account: mbox per folder + manifest.json in a ZIP (PST-REQ-151).
post.description: Needs a fresh step-up and x-postroom-csrf: 1. One active export per account: a second call while one is pending or running is 409. The archive is deleted 24 h after it finishes.

get.description: Needs a fresh step-up. 409 while the export is still pending/running; 404 once done but past its 24 h expiry (the archive was swept).

404.description: Not an export of the caller, or the archive has expired.

409.description: The export is not finished yet.

patch.description: Requires If-Match with the ETag from GET. A move creates the message in the target with a new UID (and a new id), removes it from the source, and bumps both mailboxes' HIGHESTMODSEQ. Audited. Needs x-postroom-csrf: 1.

A read: nothing is stored and nothing is fetched from anywhere else.

post.description: Only once per message: marks the message $MDNSent. Audited. Needs x-postroom-csrf: 1.

get.summary: The caller's own OutboundMessage id for this mailbox message, or null (PST-T-6.7, PST-REQ-119).
get.description: Looks up the message's Message-ID header and matches it against this account's outbound queue (an indexed lookup, never a scan). outboundId is null both when the message was never sent and when it was sent by another client, not through Postroom.

get.summary: A short-lived URL of the sanitised HTML on the usercontent origin (PST-REQ-081).
get.description: The usercontent origin has no session cookie, so this mints a capability for one message of the caller, under the caller's session, valid for 15 minutes. Remote images stay blocked unless images=1, and then load only through the image proxy (PST-REQ-082). Frame the URL with sandbox and no allow-scripts/allow-same-origin.

parameters.name: images
parameters.description: 1 = the reader chose to load remote images, through the image proxy (PST-REQ-082).

post.summary: One-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) for a message that offers it (PST-REQ-110).
post.description: Sends the List-Unsubscribe-Post over HTTPS to the message's List-Unsubscribe URL, server-side, only for a message whose DMARC passed. Records the result on the sender. A mailto: unsubscribe link is returned but never sent automatically. Audited. Needs x-postroom-csrf: 1.

200.description: Whether the message offered one-click, and the outcome.

404.description: No such message.

post.summary: A configuration profile for Mail, Calendar and Contacts on this account (PST-REQ-139).
post.description: Mints one fresh app password scoped for imap+smtp+dav and embeds it in an Apple configuration profile (Content-Type application/x-apple-aspen-config). Signed as CMS SignedData when a signing certificate is configured (X-Postroom-Mobileconfig-Signed: 1); otherwise served unsigned (: 0) and iOS shows it as Unverified. Step-up and audited.

put.summary: Pin this sender to a bucket — overrides the classifier for their mail (PST-REQ-105).
put.description: A pin into Priority or People still requires the message to authenticate, exactly like the VIP rule. Audited. Needs x-postroom-csrf: 1.

post.summary: Answer this sender's new-sender badge: Allow or Block (PST-REQ-106).
post.description: Allow treats the sender as a known contact, so a directly-addressed message from them can reach Priority. Block routes their future mail to Junk. Either clears the $NewSender badge on their already-filed mail. Audited. Needs x-postroom-csrf: 1.
